title: Settling a Micro Market Invoice Well Before It Falls Due
content:
A client of the Unattended Micro Market Program settling a micro market settlement invoice well before it falls due is given a discount on what it tenders, and how regularly it has settled over the trailing year settles how deep that discount is.

## How the days to run are counted

The day the invoice was raised is read from the equipment line the settlement invoice carries, the equipment lease being raised with the invoice itself. The days the invoice still has to run before it falls due are the payment terms printed against the market format less the days elapsed since that day.

## Conditions and discounts

**The deep prompt discount of 1.5 per cent** is given where the settlement invoice the client is settling still has at or above 15 days to run before it falls due, and the client settled at or above 3 market settlement invoices over the twelve months to the day the payment is taken.

**The light prompt discount of 0.75 per cent** is given where the invoice still has at or above 15 days to run before it falls due, and the client settled below 3 market settlement invoices over those twelve months.

**Where the invoice has fewer than 15 days to run before it falls due**, no prompt-settlement discount is given.

## The boundaries

The early-settlement days figure is 15: an invoice with exactly 15 days to run is at or above it, and an invoice with 14 days to run is below it. The regular-settler count is 3 settlement payments over the trailing twelve months: exactly 3 meets it, 2 does not.

*Hypothetical.* An invoice raised 8 days ago on a format whose payment terms are 30 calendar days still has 22 days to run; where the client settled 4 invoices over the trailing year, 1.5 per cent is taken off. Where the client settled only 1, 0.75 per cent is taken off. An invoice raised 20 days ago on the same terms has 10 days to run and earns no discount.
